title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the post-1983 manuscript on 'cohomological properties of maps in (Cat)'. That project grows out of Pursuing Stacks and leads into Les Dérivateurs. Grothendieck is organising a dictionary of classes of functors f : X -> Y, written right-to-left on the page, using topological and algebro-geometric vocabulary. The page has four parts.

(1) Top-left diagram: the comma construction. Let F(Y) be the arrow category Y^{Delta^1}, with its two projections to Y and to a second copy Y'. Then Fib(f) = F(Y) x_{Y'} X, a pullback square. Concretely, Fib(f) is the comma category whose objects are pairs (x, b : y -> f(x)).
- f^b : Fib(f) -> Y sends (x, b) to y. It is a Grothendieck fibration.
- Its fibre over y is y\X, the category of pairs (x, y -> f(x)). This is the category of elements of the copresheaf x |-> Hom(y, f(x)), hence 'discretely cofibered over X'.
- f^b is 'not yet Serre': the transition functors between fibres need not be weak equivalences.
- mu_f : X -> Fib(f), x |-> (x, id_{f(x)}), is a monomorphism and f = f^b o mu_f.
- rho_f : Fib(f) -> X, (x, b) |-> x, is a retraction with rho_f o mu_f = id. A direct computation gives Hom((x', b), mu_f x) = Hom(x', x), so rho_f is left adjoint to mu_f and rho_f is a 'homotopism' (it has an adjoint).
- rho_f is an opfibration whose fibres Y/f(x) have a final object, hence are aspherical and discretely fibered over Y. That is why he calls it a 'trivial Serre cofibering retraction'.
So every functor factors as (mono, section of a trivial cofibration-homotopism) followed by a fibration. This is the free-fibration / path-object factorisation in Cat.

(2) The central cross: a table of classes.
- Horizontal axis: smooth <-> fibration | cofibration <-> proper.
- Upper row (the 'Serre' versions): smooth Serre, Serre fibration, Serre, Serre cofibration, proper Serre.
- Trivial versions: 'Serre ∩ W = trivial Serre', where W is the class of weak equivalences.
- 'Serre' should be read as 'W-locally constant': fibres are homotopy fibres and transition maps are weak equivalences, i.e. the hypothesis of Quillen's Theorem B.
- Vertical axis, below the cross: mono and discrete.
- Mono: open immersions = sieves (cribles). These correspond to functors X^o -> Delta^1, with Y the preimage of 1, i.e. to Crib(X). Closed immersions = cosieves. These correspond to functors X -> Delta^1 = [∅ -> {∅}], with Y = phi^{-1}(1) = X_1, i.e. to Cocrib(X).
- Discrete: discrete fibrations correspond to presheaves (X^hat); discrete cofibrations correspond to copresheaves (X^check).
- The duality X |-> X^o exchanges the left and right halves.
- In this page's convention, sieves (open immersions) sit under smooth/fibration. The defining condition for smooth is then that the fibre inclusion E_b -> b\E be aspherical, universally under base change. Fibrations satisfy this, since E_b -> b\E has an adjoint.

(3) Mapping-cylinder factorisation (dual to (1)).
- f = lambda_f o f^natural, with f^natural : Y -> C(f) an open immersion.
- C(f) is the collage (cograph) of the profunctor of f: the disjoint union of Y and X, with Y as a sieve.
- lambda_f : C(f) -> X is epi, sending y |-> f(y) and x |-> x.
- lambda_f has a closed section sigma_f and is a homotopism, since it is adjoint to sigma_f.
- Dually, C'(f) = C(f^o)^o gives the factorisation (closed immersion, retraction with open section).
- The previous page also gives the cone C(Y) and the co-cone C'(Y).

(4) Bottom remarks.
- discrete ∩ Serre = étale covering. These are functors corresponding to locally constant presheaves, i.e. presheaves inverting all arrows. Equivalently: smooth ∩ proper Serre with discrete ('étale') fibres.
- mono ∩ Serre = sieve that is also a cosieve = disjoint summand, i.e. a union of connected components.
- discrete ∩ trivial Serre = iso: weakly contractible discrete fibres are singletons.
- NB, positive part: proper with discrete fibres implies a discrete cofibration; smooth with discrete fibres implies a discrete fibration.
- NB, negative part: these do not force mono. Also proper ∩ fibration does not imply cofibration, and smooth ∩ cofibration does not imply fibration, giving non-trivial examples.

Check of the positive part of the NB: base-change to Delta^1. Asphericity of F(0) -> 0\E forces each object over 1 to receive exactly one arrow from the fibre over 0. That is exactly the unique cartesian lift, so the claim holds.

Purpose. The page sets up the 'six-functor-like' dictionary (smooth / proper, open / closed, étale) for Cat with respect to the basic localizer W, as preparation for cohomological base-change statements.
errors: The equation 'discrete ∩ Serre = smooth ∩ proper Serre' is false as first written: smooth ∩ proper Serre is much larger. Grothendieck corrected it by inserting 'étale' (discrete fibres). The intended statement is 'étale coverings = smooth ∩ proper Serre with discrete fibres'.

'discrete' in the NB is ambiguous. It must mean 'with discrete fibres', not 'discrete fibration', for the implications 'proper ∩ discrete ⇒ cofibration' and 'smooth ∩ discrete ⇒ fibration' to be non-tautological. With that reading they are correct (checked by base change to Delta^1).
Smooth/proper conventions here (sieves smooth, fibrations smooth) are opposite to some later expositions. This is a convention issue, not an error, but readers should beware.

Minor notational inconsistencies: the top diagram leaves Y' versus Y unexplained; the open-immersion description uses phi^{-1}(1) on X^o and psi^{-1}(0) on X, which is consistent only via the canonical isomorphism Delta_1^o ≅ Delta_1 that he notes.

ideas.what: Factorisation f = f^b o mu_f through the comma category Fib(f) = F(Y) x_Y X: a fibration preceded by a fully faithful right adjoint section of a trivial opfibration
ideas.modern_name: free (Grothendieck) fibration on a functor / path-object factorisation in Cat
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Street (1974, Fibrations and Yoneda's lemma in a 2-category); J. Gray
ideas.where_published: comparable comma constructions in Pursuing Stacks (asphericity / Theorem A discussions); exact form unsure

ideas.what: Mapping-cylinder factorisation via collage C(f): open immersion followed by a homotopism with closed section; dual C'(f) = C(f^o)^o; cones C(Y), C'(Y)
ideas.modern_name: collage / cograph mapping cylinder in Cat
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used by Thomason and Cisinski
ideas.where_published: cylinder-type constructions appear in Pursuing Stacks; exact form unsure

ideas.what: Sieves as open immersions and cosieves as closed immersions, classified by functors to Delta^1 (Crib(X), Cocrib(X)); discrete (co)fibrations correspond to (co)presheaves
ideas.modern_name: sieves/cosieves; Delta^1 as classifier; Grothendieck construction for presheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 4: open/closed subtopoi) and standard category theory

ideas.what: Table smooth / fibration / cofibration / proper with 'Serre' (W-locally constant) and 'trivial' (∩W) versions, organised by the duality X -> X^o
ideas.modern_name: W-smooth and W-proper functors; locally constant (Quillen B) fibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs); developed by Cisinski and Maltsiniotis
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks; Les Dérivateurs; Maltsiniotis, Astérisque 301

ideas.what: Étale coverings = discrete ∩ Serre = smooth ∩ proper Serre with discrete fibres; mono ∩ Serre = disjoint summand; discrete ∩ trivial Serre = iso

ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Quillen; Gabriel–Zisman for coverings of groupoids)

missed.claim: Explicit small lemma: a W-smooth functor (universal asphericity of E_b -> b\E) with discrete fibres is a discrete fibration, dually for proper and cofibration. Together with the étale = smooth ∩ proper ∩ discrete-fibre identification, this forms a compact 'étale morphism' dictionary for Cat. It may not be stated in this form in the literature, though it is easy.
missed.quote: NB proper ∩ discrete ⇒ cofib, smooth ∩ discrete ⇒ fibration but does not imply mono
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean intrinsic homotopical characterisation of (co)presheaves among W-smooth/proper functors, mirroring 'étale = smooth + unramified'. Minor, but handy for six-functor formalisms on Cat / ∞-categories.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a well-organised dictionary of mostly standard facts. It contains the comma and collage factorisations, the sieve = open / cosieve = closed analogy, and smooth/proper with Serre and trivial variants, all present in Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs and the Cisinski–Maltsiniotis literature. The only slightly non-routine item is the discrete-fibre characterisation in the NB, which is easy.
transcription_corrections: Top diagram: 'F(f)(Y)' should be 'F(Y)', the arrow category of Y. The vertical arrow under Fib(f) is labelled rho_f (or p_f), and a dashed curved arrow mu_f goes back up. The bottom row reads Y' <- X with label f.
Closed immersion line: 'X -φ-> Δ^1 = [∅ -> {∅}]', with 0 and 1 written above ∅ and {∅}.
Mono row: a crossed-out word under 'mono' is illegible.
Bottom: 'discrete ∩ Serre (= étale covering) = smooth ∩ proper étale Serre', where 'étale,' is an insertion above the line.
Bottom: the crossed-out start 'mono ∩ Serre' is followed by '= open ∩ closed imm = disjoint summand'.
Bottom: 'discrete ∩ trivial Serre = iso'; the crossed-out word is 'trivial'.
Last lines: '...and proper ∩ fibr does not imply cofibration (not trivial), smooth ∩ cofibr not imply fibration (not trivial)'.
